title: Simplify Path
statement_short: Given an absolute Unix-style file path starting with a slash, transform it into its simplified canonical path. Double dots '..' navigate up a directory, single dots '.' refer to the current directory, and multiple consecutive slashes are treated as a single slash.
constraints: 1 <= path.length <= 3000, path consists of English letters, digits, period '.', slash '/', or underscore '_'
hint: Small path length (<= 3000) permits splitting by slashes and processing directory tokens sequentially.
why_not: Right: Stack processes path directory tokens separated by slashes, popping when encountering '..' to navigate back up directories in O(n) time and O(n) space. Not Two Pointers: Scanning pointers cannot handle multi-level directory backtrack operations easily without LIFO history tracking. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Directory navigation depends on relative path history rather than set membership. Not Trie: Prefix trees store hierarchical filesystem structures, but parsing a single path string relies on stack token management.
